text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A parliamentary commission investigating a security scandal finishes its enquiries with prisoners in Istanbul. The commission will go to the southeast to question inmates there who could have links with the scandal.
- Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan refuses to sign a packet of measures prepared by the National Security Council to counter Islamist movements.
- The general secretary of the Turkish armed forces says the military will only be in harmony with those who support the secular principles of Ataturk, the founder of the Turkish republic.
- The National Security Council gives two months to the Islamist-led government to implement a package of measures to fight Islamist movements.
- A security scandal linking senior police officials with underground gangs has not faded in the four months since it emerged.
- Turkish women will celebrate the 73rd anniversary of the end of the Caliphate and the introduction of secularist measures by leaving flowers at the statue of Ataturk in Taksim Square.
- Israeli readywear companies seek the possibility of joint ventures with Turkish firms.
- Erbakan begins visits to opposition leaders in order to dispel mounting political tension.
